The quarter-ellipse above is defined by the parametric equations 

$$
x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $\theta ?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

In our case, $a=4$ and $b=8.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the *full* ellipse are

$$
x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a quarter-ellipse, we associate the parameter $\theta $ with the parameter angle on the unit circle with coordinates $(x/a,y/b)$. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186152190/plots/8d8562e0b85cd9796c9d4344-solution.png)

We can see that if we restrict $\theta $ to $[0,\frac{\pi }{2}]$, we get the quarter-ellipse.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the quarter-ellipse are 

$$
x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,\frac{\pi }{2}].
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186152190/plots/a247080b3413877fcbe10e17-prompt.png)

The semi-ellipse above is defined by the parametric equations 

$$
x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $\theta ?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

In our case, $a=4$ and $b=8.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the *full* ellipse are

$$
x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a semi-ellipse, we associate the parameter $\theta $ with the parameter angle on the unit circle with coordinates $(x/a,y/b)$. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186152190/plots/a247080b3413877fcbe10e17-solution.png)

We can see that if we restrict $\theta $ to $[0,\pi ]$, we get the semi-ellipse.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the semi-ellipse are 

$$
x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,\pi ].
$$

x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +4,\,y=8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -3.

question.:question/worked-solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +h,\,y=b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +k,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

In our case, the ellipse is centered at the point $(4,-3),$ $a=4$ and $b=8.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the *full* ellipse are

$$
x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +4,\,y=8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -3,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a quarter-ellipse, we associate the parameter $\theta $ with the parameter angle on the unit circle with coordinates $((x-h)/a,(y-k)/b)$.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186152190/plots/4400dc46ec35434ed065b42f-solution.png)

We can see that if we restrict $\theta $ to $[0,\frac{\pi }{2}]$, we get the quarter-ellipse.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the quarter-ellipse are 

$$
x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +4,\,y=8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -3,\,\theta \in [0,\frac{\pi }{2}].
$$
